title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (October 2026 data) + the quarterly cut, 4:00 p.m. ET — four days after the CR expires
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200) by the tic-monthly-2026-10-16 initial-research adjacency sweep — its 2026 table puts December's monthly release AND the quarterly cut (nonfinancial firms, derivatives, portfolio claims and liabilities at end of previous quarter) both on the 15th, with gross external debt separately on the 31st, under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. Reference month October 2026 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. Corroborated mechanically: with federal holidays excluded the 11th business day of December 2026 is 12-15 EXACTLY (offset +0 on the page's '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule), the same convention that reproduces 22 of 24 published 2026-27 dates. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-monthly-2026-10-16 initial research (2026-09-08) and proposed EARLY, ahead of its November sibling's turn, for one reason: it is the TIC release exposed to a funding lapse, and this lane now has the precedent measured rather than feared. The October 2025 release did not slip — it was CANCELLED, its data folded into 2025-11-18 alongside September's, in Treasury's own words ('data for August (delayed by the partial shutdown of the federal government) and September 2025', press release sb0317). Treasury's release-dates page carries the standing notice that a date is revised when federal offices in Washington D.C. are closed. PL 119-103 funds agencies only through 2026-12-11 (already tracked as cr-expiry-2026-12-11 and government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11), so this release sits FOUR DAYS inside the lapse window — the same relative position 2025-10-16 held when it was cancelled. Getting it onto the calendar now is what lets its own session assess that exposure with lead time instead of discovering it at D-3. Impact LOW on the standing grounds (16:00 ET, six-week-old data, no macro-keyed playbook); the existence risk is a scheduling fact, not a trading edge, and nothing here licenses an entry.
